A_target.statement:
The [[Definition:Fundamental Group|fundamental group]] of the circle is:
:$\map {\pi_1} {\Bbb S^1, 1} \cong \Z$
with the class of $t \mapsto e^{2 \pi i n t}$ corresponding to $n$.

B_source.statement:
Let $p: \R \to \Bbb S^1$, $\map p s = e^{2 \pi i s}$.
Then every [[Definition:Path (Topology)|path]] in $\Bbb S^1$ has a unique lift to $\R$ with a given starting point, and homotopies of paths lift uniquely to homotopies.

substitutions.loops at 1: paths in R from 0 to an integer

object_map.reformulation: Measure a loop by the endpoint of its lift to the covering line.

validity_conditions: The fibre over 1 is the discrete set Z, so lifted homotopies fix the endpoint.
R is contractible, which gives injectivity.
proof_plan:
For a loop $\gamma$ at $1$, lift it to $\tilde \gamma$ starting at $0$.
Then $\map {\tilde \gamma} 1 \in \map {p^{-1} } 1 = \Z$; define $\map {\deg} {\sqbrk \gamma} = \map {\tilde \gamma} 1$.

A homotopy of loops lifts to a homotopy of paths whose endpoint moves continuously in the discrete set $\Z$, hence is fixed.
So $\deg$ is well-defined.

The lift of $\gamma \cdot \delta$ is $\tilde \gamma$ followed by $\map {\tilde \gamma} 1 + \tilde \delta$, so $\deg$ is a homomorphism.
It is surjective, as $t \mapsto e^{2 \pi i n t}$ lifts to $t \mapsto n t$.
